Description: Review Priority Model routes some groups of applicants to Enhanced Review or Recommend Decline more often than comparable applicants
Cause: Trained on past adjudicator decisions; features such as FSA and employer may act as proxies for protected characteristics; no direct demographic data to test with; thin-file and newcomer applicants underrepresented
Potential Impact: Denial of credit to eligible applicants; human rights complaints; supervisory scrutiny; reputational harm
Affected Stakeholders: Applicants (newcomers; Indigenous; racialized; older; rural and lower-income); Northstar; regulators
Existing Controls: Enterprise model risk policy; existing credit decision review and complaints process; design intent to exclude age; name; language and marital status from model features
Control Gap: Feature exclusion not verified (OI-03); no agreed fairness metrics or thresholds (OI-07); no approved proxy-testing method; lawfulness of inferring protected attributes unconfirmed (OI-09)
Recommended Control: Verify feature exclusion and audit FSA and employer as proxies before build freeze; run pre-deployment fairness testing using geographic and name-based analysis plus synthetic matched pairs; monitor monthly after launch against committee-approved thresholds
KRI/KPI: Ratio of Enhanced Review and Recommend Decline rates between proxy-inferred groups and a reference group (0.80 screening ratio proposed; not a Canadian legal standard); matched-pair outcome gap
Escalation Trigger: Ratio below 0.80 in any month or below 0.90 for two consecutive months: notify AI Governance Committee within 5 business days and pause any rollout expansion
ISO 42001 Mapping: Cl. 6.1.4 and 8.4 (AI system impact assessment); Annex A.7 (data for AI systems)
EU AI Act Relevance: Art. 10(2) (bias examination and mitigation); Art. 9; Annex III point 5(b) (creditworthiness). Benchmark only
Intake Reference: Sections F; J; K; OI-03; OI-07; OI-09

Description: Score or recommended path is wrong so risky files receive Standard Review or sound files receive Recommend Decline
Cause: Labels reflect past decisions; declined applicants have no repayment outcome (reject inference); six-year training window may not match current conditions; outcomes lag 6 to 12 months so errors surface late
Potential Impact: Credit losses; wrongful declines; inconsistent review depth; loss of adjudicator trust
Existing Controls: Enterprise model risk policy requires independent validation; adjudicators review every file
Control Gap: Beacon validation not yet performed; reject inference approach not documented; no agreed performance tolerances; no backtesting plan
Recommended Control: Independent validation by Model Risk Management before pilot including out-of-time and segment testing; documented reject inference approach; agreed performance tolerances; quarterly backtesting as outcomes mature
KRI/KPI: Gini (rank-ordering) versus validation baseline; loss rate of Standard Review path versus Enhanced Review path; performance by segment
Escalation Trigger: Gini falls more than 10 percent relative to baseline or a segment gap exceeds tolerance: notify Model Risk Management within 5 business days
ISO 42001 Mapping: Cl. 8.2; Annex A.6 (AI system life cycle)
EU AI Act Relevance: Art. 15 (accuracy and robustness); Art. 9. Benchmark only

AI Risk: Automation bias and anchoring on the recommendation
Description: Adjudicators follow the recommended path without forming an independent view so Recommend Decline becomes the de facto decision
Cause: Time pressure (Beacon targets 20 percent faster handling); recommendation is visible before the adjudicator forms a view; scores appear authoritative; no training on model limitations
Potential Impact: Wrongful declines at scale; loss of the human review that keeps Beacon assistive; tier rises to Critical if concordance exceeds 90 percent
Existing Controls: Adjudicators hold delegated lending authority and can override any recommendation
Control Gap: No rationale requirement; override tracking not built (OI-06); no training on model limits or automation bias; no concordance baseline
Recommended Control: Written rationale required when following Recommend Decline; blind re-review of a random sample where the adjudicator decides before seeing the recommendation; concordance and override monitoring by adjudicator and team; training before pilot
KRI/KPI: Concordance rate with Recommend Decline; override rate; median review time on Recommend Decline files versus baseline
Escalation Trigger: Team concordance above 90 percent over a month or override rate below 3 percent: AI Governance Office review and tier reassessment (see methodology sensitivity table)
ISO 42001 Mapping: Annex A.9 (use of AI systems); Cl. 7.2 (competence)
EU AI Act Relevance: Art. 14(4)(b) (awareness of automation bias); Art. 26 (deployer oversight). Benchmark only

AI Risk: Human oversight exists in name only
Description: Adjudicators lack the time; skills; authority or evidence trail to challenge Beacon so oversight cannot be demonstrated to auditors or supervisors
Cause: Override and rationale capture not built; training covers credit judgment but not model limits; review time shrinks after rollout; no defined rule for when override or escalation is mandatory
Potential Impact: Failure of the primary safeguard; inability to evidence oversight; adverse audit or supervisory findings
Existing Controls: Delegated lending authority; logging of inputs; scores and adjudicator actions is designed into the Workbench
Control Gap: Override and rationale capture not built (OI-06); mandatory override and escalation rules undefined; no capacity monitoring; no fallback if logging fails
Recommended Control: Build override and rationale capture before pilot; define mandatory override and escalation triggers in the Human Oversight Framework; monitor time per file and queue pressure; suspend the Recommend Decline display if logging is down for more than 24 hours
KRI/KPI: Percent of files with follow or override rationale captured (target 100 percent for Recommend Decline); median review time per file versus baseline; percent of adjudicators trained
Escalation Trigger: Capture rate below 98 percent in a week or logging outage above 24 hours: suspend Recommend Decline display and notify AI Governance Office
ISO 42001 Mapping: Annex A.9; Annex A.6 (operation and monitoring); Cl. 9.1

Description: Applicants or adjudicators cannot get a meaningful reason for a recommendation; LLM summaries may state things the source documents do not support
Cause: Reason codes not validated as faithful to the model; LLM summaries are not explainable; adverse-action reasons could be lifted from the Beacon score; applicants are not told AI is involved
Potential Impact: Unfair or non-compliant adverse-action notices; inability to answer complaints or supervisor questions; loss of applicant trust
Existing Controls: Adverse-action reasons must come from the adjudicator's own assessment and may not cite the Beacon score alone; reason codes plus SHAP explanations for the Review Priority Model
Control Gap: Reason code faithfulness not validated; no source-citation standard for LLM summaries; applicant disclosure position unresolved (OI-01; OI-09)
Recommended Control: Validate reason codes during independent validation; require every LLM summary statement to link to a source document location and sample-audit citation accuracy; adverse-action standard citing adjudicator-assessed factors; Legal to conclude on applicant disclosure
KRI/KPI: Percent of LLM summary statements with a valid source citation in sample audit (98 percent proposed); percent of adverse-action notices citing adjudicator-assessed factors; complaints citing unexplained decisions
Escalation Trigger: Citation validity below 98 percent in any monthly sample: disable LLM summarization using the feature flag pending review
NIST AI RMF Mapping: MEASURE 2.8; MEASURE 2.9; GenAI Profile risk: Confabulation
ISO 42001 Mapping: Annex A.8 (information for interested parties); Annex A.6 (documentation)
EU AI Act Relevance: Art. 13 (transparency to deployers); Art. 86 (explanation of individual decisions). Benchmark only
Intake Reference: Sections E; G; K; OI-01; OI-09

AI Risk: Model drift and degradation over time
Description: Applicant population; economic conditions or products change so scores lose accuracy or shift outcomes for some groups
Cause: Six-year training window; changing rates and employment conditions; product or channel changes; outcome lag delays performance evidence
Potential Impact: Accuracy and fairness degrade unnoticed; credit losses; unplanned redevelopment
Existing Controls: Enterprise model change process with re-validation
Control Gap: Drift monitoring not built; no thresholds set; fairness not monitored separately from accuracy; retraining triggers untested
Recommended Control: Monthly stability monitoring of score and top features; fairness indicators tracked on the same cadence; quarterly backtesting as outcomes mature; documented retraining triggers and re-validation
KRI/KPI: Population Stability Index on score and top features (0.10 watch and 0.25 investigate are common industry conventions); fairness ratio trend
Escalation Trigger: PSI above 0.25 on the score or any top-10 feature for two consecutive months: open model review and notify Model Risk Management

AI Risk: Sensitive personal information exposed through the LLM vendor
Description: Pay stubs; bank statements and adjudicator notes sent to the vendor-hosted LLM are retained; accessed or disclosed beyond what Northstar intends
Cause: Vendor default 30-day retention for abuse monitoring; zero-retention addendum not agreed; sub-processors unknown; full documents sent when only some fields are needed; vendor training prohibition not yet verified
Potential Impact: Privacy breach affecting applicants; breach notification and record-keeping duties; regulator and public scrutiny; loss of customer trust
Affected Stakeholders: Applicants; Privacy Office; Northstar; regulators (OPC and Quebec CAI)
Existing Controls: Canadian-region dedicated tenancy; contract draft prohibits vendor training on Northstar data (not yet verified); logging of prompts and outputs with personal information controls
Control Gap: Zero-retention addendum not agreed (OI-04); sub-processor list not received (OI-05); no input minimization or redaction; vendor security assessment not started (OI-04)
Recommended Control: Zero-retention and no-training terms signed before pilot; send only the documents and fields needed and mask identifiers such as SIN and full account numbers before sending; obtain and approve the sub-processor list; vendor security assessment before pilot; scheduled scan of prompt logs for unmasked identifiers
KRI/KPI: Unmasked identifiers found in prompt log scans (target 0); vendor retention exceptions found in audit (target 0); percent of required vendor privacy terms executed (100 percent before pilot)
Monitoring Frequency: Weekly log scan in pilot; monthly after; annual vendor audit
Escalation Trigger: Any confirmed unmasked identifier sent to the vendor or retention beyond contract: open a privacy incident within 24 hours and Privacy Officer assesses breach reporting duties (PIPEDA real risk of significant harm test; Law 25 for Quebec residents; Legal to confirm)
NIST AI RMF Mapping: MEASURE 2.10; MANAGE 3.1; GenAI Profile risk: Data Privacy
ISO 42001 Mapping: Annex A.7 (data for AI systems); Annex A.10 (third-party and customer relationships)
EU AI Act Relevance: Art. 10 (data governance); Art. 15. Benchmark only; PIPEDA and Law 25 are the binding privacy regimes
Intake Reference: Sections F; G; L; N; OI-04; OI-05

AI Risk: Personal information used beyond its original consented purpose
Description: Historical application data; adjudicator notes and uploaded documents are reused for model training and LLM processing in ways applicants did not agree to or expect
Cause: Consent wording predates AI; training on six years of historical data; purpose limitation not assessed; retention periods assumed rather than confirmed
Potential Impact: Non-compliance with PIPEDA consent and limiting-use principles; Law 25 exposure for Quebec residents; complaints to the OPC; forced retraining or data deletion
Existing Controls: Consent collected at application; Privacy Office consulted at intake; Quebec applicants excluded from pilot
Control Gap: PIA not started (OI-02); consent and purpose limitation not confirmed (OI-01); retention period assumed at 7 years; no procedure for access requests or challenges that involve Beacon outputs
Recommended Control: Complete the PIA before build freeze with a documented lawful basis for each data source; Legal decision on consent wording and applicant notice; confirm retention and deletion rules for scores; prompts and summaries; define how access requests and challenges involving Beacon outputs are handled
KRI/KPI: Percent of Beacon data elements with documented purpose and lawful basis (100 percent before pilot); open high-rated PIA findings (0 at approval gate); access requests involving Beacon answered within 30 days (100 percent)
Escalation Trigger: High-rated PIA finding unresolved at an approval gate: gate held; any complaint alleging unconsented AI use: notify Chief Privacy Officer and Legal within 2 business days
ISO 42001 Mapping: Cl. 4.2 (interested parties and legal requirements); Annex A.7
Intake Reference: Sections F; I; OI-01; OI-02; OI-09

AI Risk: LLM vendor changes; fails or becomes hard to leave
Description: Meridian updates the model without notice; suffers an outage or breach; changes sub-processors; or Northstar cannot exit without losing the summarization capability
Cause: Vendor controls the model; change-notice; audit-rights and incident-notice terms still under negotiation (OI-04); same vendor shortlisted for another use case (OI-10); no exit test
Potential Impact: Summaries change behaviour without validation; service disruption; delayed breach notice; costly forced migration
Affected Stakeholders: Adjudicators; applicants; Vendor Risk; Procurement; Northstar
Existing Controls: Model version pinned at contract (terms not final); LLM can be switched off independently by feature flag; enterprise third-party risk process
Control Gap: Change-notice; audit-rights and 24-hour incident notice not agreed (OI-04); concentration not assessed (OI-10); no regression test for vendor updates; fallback runbook not written
Recommended Control: Executed contract with audit rights; 30-day model change notice and 24-hour incident notice before pilot; regression test on a fixed test set before accepting any vendor model update; annual vendor review including sub-processor changes; tested fallback runbook and 90-day exit plan
KRI/KPI: Unannounced vendor model changes detected by canary test set (target 0); vendor SLA breaches per quarter; percent of required contract controls executed (100 percent before pilot); fallback runbook tested in last 12 months (yes or no)
Monitoring Frequency: Daily canary test; quarterly vendor review
Escalation Trigger: Canary test results change without a vendor change notice: disable LLM summarization via feature flag and notify Vendor Risk and Model Risk Management the same day
ISO 42001 Mapping: Annex A.10 (third-party and customer relationships); Cl. 8.1 (operational control)
EU AI Act Relevance: Art. 25 (responsibilities along the AI value chain); Art. 26. Benchmark only
Intake Reference: Sections G; N; OI-04; OI-05; OI-10

AI Risk: Prompt injection and manipulated output through uploaded documents
Description: An applicant or third party hides instructions in a pay stub or bank statement so the summary omits inconsistencies; overstates income or misleads the adjudicator
Cause: The LLM reads untrusted document content as input; summaries influence adjudicator judgement; output is displayed in the Workbench
Potential Impact: Fraudulent applications look clean; loss of confidence in summaries; credit losses; injected content shown in the Workbench
Existing Controls: LLM has no tool calling; no write access and no retrieval beyond the single application; output shown to adjudicators only
Control Gap: No document sanitization or injection detection; no adversarial testing; no cross-check of LLM figures against structured data; output rendering not reviewed
Recommended Control: Treat all document content as untrusted; strip hidden text and non-visible layers before summarization; render output as plain text only; cross-check key figures (income and balances) against structured data and flag mismatches; red team testing before pilot and annually; keep tools and write access disabled
KRI/KPI: Injection attempts detected per month; open high-rated red team findings (0 at approval gate); percent of summaries where key figures disagree with structured data
Monitoring Frequency: Monthly; red team annually and after major changes
Escalation Trigger: Any confirmed successful injection that changed a summary: disable LLM summarization via feature flag and open a security incident the same day
NIST AI RMF Mapping: MEASURE 2.7; MANAGE 4.1; GenAI Profile risk: Information Security
ISO 42001 Mapping: Annex A.6 (verification and validation); Annex A.9
EU AI Act Relevance: Art. 15(5) (resilience against manipulation of inputs and outputs). Benchmark only. OWASP LLM01 (Prompt Injection) and LLM05 (Improper Output Handling); verify numbering against the current OWASP list

AI Risk: Cyber attacks on the model; its data and its pipeline
Description: Attackers or insiders poison training data; steal or probe the model; tamper with scores or stored artifacts; or compromise privileged accounts
Cause: Model and data pipeline are new attack surface; threat model still in progress; privileged access for model engineers; no integrity checks on data or artifacts; applicants can probe outputs by resubmitting applications
Potential Impact: Manipulated or leaked scores; theft of the model; exposure of personal information; undetected changes to decision support
Affected Stakeholders: Applicants; Northstar; Cybersecurity; Model Risk Management
Existing Controls: Role-based access; privileged access management for engineers; SIEM logging; enterprise incident process
Control Gap: Threat model incomplete; no integrity checks on training data or model artifacts; no monitoring for probing or extraction; no AI-specific incident playbook
Recommended Control: Complete the threat model before build freeze; least-privilege access with quarterly recertification; hash and sign training datasets and model artifacts with change logging; detect abnormal query or resubmission patterns; write and test an AI incident playbook
KRI/KPI: Overdue privileged access reviews (target 0); unauthorized changes to model artifacts (target 0); anomalous resubmission or query alerts per month; AI playbook exercise completed (yes or no)
Monitoring Frequency: Continuous alerting; quarterly access review; annual playbook exercise
Escalation Trigger: Unapproved change to a model artifact or training data: suspend the model and open a security incident immediately; confirmed extraction attempt: notify CISO within 24 hours
EU AI Act Relevance: Art. 15 (accuracy; robustness and cybersecurity). Benchmark only. OWASP LLM04 (Data and Model Poisoning) for the LLM component; verify numbering

AI Risk: Non-compliance with applicable regulation and supervisory expectations
Description: Beacon is deployed or scaled without meeting binding obligations (privacy; human rights; model risk management; consumer credit) or without required supervisory engagement
Cause: No AI-specific federal statute; obligations spread across several regimes; OSFI E-23 scope and timing not confirmed; Legal not yet consulted; regulator engagement decision open
Potential Impact: Supervisory findings; enforcement or remediation orders; forced suspension; reputational harm
Existing Controls: Interim AI policy; enterprise compliance framework; Compliance and Privacy consulted at intake
Control Gap: Legal not yet consulted (OI-09); no register mapping obligations to controls; E-23 alignment not assessed; regulator engagement undecided
Recommended Control: Regulatory obligations register with named owners; Legal review at each lifecycle gate; E-23 alignment assessment; documented decision on regulator engagement before pilot approval; track regulatory change including EU AI Act timing
KRI/KPI: Open Legal items past due (0 at gate); percent of obligations with an owner and a mapped control (100 percent); regulatory changes unassessed after 60 days (0)
Escalation Trigger: Blocking Legal item open at a gate: gate held and Executive Risk Committee informed; supervisory inquiry about Beacon: notify Chief Compliance Officer and Legal immediately
EU AI Act Relevance: Arts. 8 to 15 as a design benchmark; Art. 17 (quality management system). Benchmark only
